docs/reference/build-targets.html.title: Build Targets | Passel
docs/reference/build-targets.html.summary: Build Targets The build is an Atom project in _atom/. Run dotnet tool restore once, then run a target from the repository root with dotnet atom <Target>. To list the targets and their parameters, run dotnet run --project _atom -- --help (the help of the tool itself describes the tool, not the targets). With the tool installed globally, atom <Target> also works from PowerShell and cmd. Parameters can be passed on the command line (--mobile-app-flavor production), or set in _atom/appsettings.json. Secrets are read from Azure Key Vault (invex-passel). Development Target Description SetupDevEnvironment Checks the tools you need, Docker, and the HTTPS development certificate. Creates src/mobile_app/.env, then restores npm and Flutter packages. Test Runs TestWebApi, TestChromeExtension and TestMobileApp TestWebApi dotnet test on the Web API unit tests, then on the integration tests, which start PostgreSQL and Azurite in Docker containers TestChromeExtension Type-checks every member of the npm workspace (the shared packages, the extension and the web app) and runs their Vitest suites with coverage; keeps the lcov reports in atom-publish/ChromeExtensionCoverage TestMobileApp flutter analyze and flutter test --coverage; keeps the lcov report in atom-publish/MobileAppCoverage BuildDocs Builds this site into _site/ and atom-publish/GeneratedDocs ServeDocs Builds the docs and serves them at http://localhost:8080 Gen Regenerates the GitHub workflows and Dependabot configuration under .github/ from _atom/IBuild.cs; see Continuous Integration Release builds Target Output Parameters BuildWebApi Published API, in atom-publish/Invex.Passel.WebApi None BuildChromeExtension atom-publish/ChromeExtension/chrome-extension.zip api-base-url-production (the extension calls <url>/api/packets), chrome-extension-client-id BuildWebApp The web app's static site (landing, privacy and terms pages, and the app), in atom-publish/WebApp. It holds no environment's values: the app reads the API's address and the Google client id from /app/config.json, which the web image writes when it starts; see Hosting None BuildMobileAppAndroid A debug APK (development) or a signed, obfuscated app bundle plus symbols (production), in atom-publish/android mobile-app-flavor, api-base-url-production / api-base-url-development, server-client-id, mobile-app-client-id, plus the android-keystore-* secrets for production PublishImages The API image (passel-webapi, from the .NET SDK's container support) and the web image (passel-web, Caddy with the site BuildWebApp built and an entrypoint that configures it from API_ORIGIN and GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID when the container starts), tagged with the version and sha-<commit>. Pushed to the registry only from refs/heads/main with push-images; otherwise loaded into the local Docker daemon as invex-games/passel-webapi and invex-games/passel-web. Runs after TestWebApi container-registry (ghcr.io), container-namespace (invex-games), push-images PublishDeployBundle The deploy bundle image (passel-deploy): the compose files and scripts in deploy/compose, FROM scratch, with the same tags and push rules as PublishImages. Runs after TestWebApi The same as PublishImages PublishDocs The site built by BuildDocs, force-pushed to the gh-pages branch for GitHub Pages github-token BuildMobileAppAndroid checks out the Flutter version in flutter-version (_atom/appsettings.json). If there's no Flutter on your PATH, it clones that version into .flutter/. Running it locally can therefore switch the version of your own Flutter SDK. The client-id parameters only take effect when they're real Google client ids (ending in .apps.googleusercontent.com). Otherwise the build logs a warning and uses the values in src/mobile_app/.env. Deployment The versions come from GitVersion (GitVersion.yml), which IBuild uses as its version and build id provider: SetupBuildInfo prints the version, and the image targets read the one it stored, so run it first locally. An image tag is the version with + and / replaced by -. A version tag already in the registry is never moved: the image targets skip a push the registry already has for the same commit, and fail when the tag names another. Target What it does Parameters ValidateCompose docker compose config over deploy/compose/compose.yaml, alone and with each override, with every profile on and the placeholders in ci.env, then checks that the web service gets API_ORIGIN=https://<API_HOST> and GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=<GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID>, then shellcheck over the deploy scripts and the web image's entrypoint (in the koalaman/shellcheck image when shellcheck isn't installed). The Validate workflow runs it on every pull request. None DeployCompose Deploys a tag to the self-hosted server: checks that the three images exist, then runs ssh to the deploy gate with deploy <tag> and the registry token on stdin. Needs the DEPLOY_SSH_KEY, DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS and GHCR_PULL_TOKEN environment variables; the DeployCompose workflow sets them. See Releasing and Deploying image-tag (blank for this build's version), migrate (default true; false for a rollback), deploy-host, deploy-user PublishAzureInfrastructure Writes the Bicep of the Azure deployment from the AppHost into atom-publish/AzureInfrastructure, without signing in to Azure. The Validate workflow runs it on every pull request. None DeployWebApi Runs aspire deploy: provisions or updates the Azure resources, builds the images with the .NET SDK's container support, runs the database migration job, then updates the API. Also attaches the Bicep as AzureInfrastructure. Needs a signed-in Azure CLI; the Deploy workflow signs in with OIDC. azure-subscription-id, azure-resource-group, azure-location, server-client-id (the Google web client id), chrome-extension-client-id, optionally api-domain and api-certificate-name, and the Parameters__encoding-alphabet environment variable PublishAzureInfrastructure and DeployWebApi belong to the legacy Azure deployment and run the Aspire CLI pinned in dotnet-tools.json (dotnet aspire). See Releasing and Deploying for the one-off Azure setup DeployWebApi needs, and Configuration for where each value ends up.

docs/reference/configuration.html.title: Configuration | Passel
docs/reference/configuration.html.summary: Configuration AppHost Parameter Secret Passed to google-client-id No The API's Authentication:Google:ClientId, and the web app's GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID google-client-secret Yes The API's Authentication:Google:ClientSecret google-extension-client-id No The API's Authentication:Google:AdditionalAudiences:0, and the extension's GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID The values are stored in the AppHost's user secrets as Parameters:<name>. In Development all three are optional and default to empty, so the dashboard doesn't prompt for them; the API then works through the Dev scheme described in Run without Google. Outside Development they're required. google-client-secret is only used locally: a published or deployed AppHost never asks for it, and the API in Azure never has it. The AppHost also gives the extension and the web app API_URL (<API https endpoint>/api/packets), runs the web app on PORT 5245, and gives the API its passel-db connection string, the passel-blobs connection string of the passel-storage resource (Azurite, in a persistent container with a data volume, so stored files survive AppHost restarts as the database does) and the web app's origin, http://localhost:5245, as Cors:AllowedOrigins:0. The API waits for the parcels container to exist before it starts. The AppHost reads one setting of its own: Key Default Description DevTunnel:AllowAnonymous true Whether the passel-api-tunnel resource lets anyone with the URL through. Set it to false (in user secrets, the git-ignored appsettings.Development.json, or the DevTunnel__AllowAnonymous environment variable) and the tunnel requires a Dev Tunnels access token, which the mobile app sends from TUNNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN; see Requiring a token. The tunnel only runs when started from the dashboard either way. Compose deployment The self-hosted deployment (Releasing and Deploying) reads every value from the stack's .env, /opt/passel/.env for production and /opt/passel-preprod/.env for a pre-prod stack beside it, whose template, with a comment on each key, is deploy/compose/.env.example; release.env, written by deploy.sh, adds PASSEL_TAG. compose.yaml gives the API, db-migrate and the web app an explicit environment built from those keys, never the whole file, so nothing else in .env reaches them. .env key Required Becomes PASSEL_TAG Set by deploy.sh The tag of the passel-webapi and passel-web images, and service.version in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES COMPOSE_FILE, COMPOSE_PROFILES Yes Which files and profiles every compose command uses: the proxy setup, and telemetry for the dashboard POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_DB No The superuser and the database PostgreSQL creates on first start (postgres, passel); POSTGRES_DB is also the database in both connection strings POSTGRES_PASSWORD Yes The superuser's password, which db-roles signs in with. PostgreSQL only sets it when the database is first created PASSEL_OWNER_DB_PASSWORD Yes The password of passel_owner, and db-migrate's ConnectionStrings__passel-db (Username=passel_owner) PASSEL_API_DB_PASSWORD Yes The password of passel_api, and the API's ConnectionStrings__passel-db (Username=passel_api). db-migrate gets Database__ApiRole=passel_api ENCODING_ALPHABET Yes Encoding__Alphabet. Never changed once ids are in use GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID Yes Authentication__Google__ClientId, and the web app's GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, which it signs in with CHROME_EXTENSION_CLIENT_ID No Authentication__Google__AdditionalAudiences__0 API_HOST Yes AllowedHosts, as <API_HOST>;localhost (the healthcheck sends localhost); the web app's API_ORIGIN, https://<API_HOST>, which it calls and allows in its policy; the edge's site for the API; the smoke check's default https://<API_HOST>/health WEB_HOST Yes The edge's site for the web app. Only the edge uses it, but the compose file requires it in every setup WEB_ORIGIN Yes Cors__AllowedOrigins__0, written as a browser sends it PROXY_TRUSTED_CIDR No ForwardedHeaders__KnownNetworks__0, with ForwardedHeaders__Enabled=true. Default <PASSEL_EDGE_ADDRESS>/32, the bundled edge (172.30.0.2/32). compose.ports.yaml replaces it with the host's addresses on the two networks, <PASSEL_EDGE_GATEWAY>/32 and <PASSEL_BACKEND_GATEWAY>/32 (172.30.0.1/32 and 172.30.1.1/32) PROXY_NETWORK With compose.external-proxy.yaml The existing Docker network the edge network becomes API_PORT, WEB_PORT No The loopback ports of compose.ports.yaml (18080, 18081) DASHBOARD_PORT No The dashboard's loopback port with the telemetry profile (18888) COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME No The project name, passel by default, which prefixes the stack's containers, networks and volumes (passel_pgdata). A second stack on the server needs another, such as passel-preprod PASSEL_BACKEND_SUBNET, PASSEL_BACKEND_GATEWAY No The backend network's subnet and gateway (172.30.1.0/24, 172.30.1.1) PASSEL_EDGE_SUBNET, PASSEL_EDGE_GATEWAY, PASSEL_EDGE_IP_RANGE No The edge network's subnet, gateway and the range other containers get addresses from (172.30.0.0/24, 172.30.0.1, 172.30.0.128/25). Not used with compose.external-proxy.yaml PASSEL_EDGE_ADDRESS No The bundled edge's fixed address (172.30.0.2), in the subnet but outside PASSEL_EDGE_IP_RANGE, and the default of PROXY_TRUSTED_CIDR PASSEL_API_ALIAS, PASSEL_WEB_ALIAS No The names the API and the web app have on the edge network, which a proxy sends requests to (passel-api, passel-web); the bundled edge gets them too. Two stacks on one external proxy network need different ones PASSEL_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT No deployment.environment in the API's and db-migrate's OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (production); preprod for a pre-prod stack. ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT stays Production in both SMOKE_URL No What deploy.sh fetches after starting a release OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS No Passed to the API and db-migrate as they are; no endpoint, no export. OTEL_SERVICE_NAME is passel-webapi and passel-migrate The compose file also sets, on the API and db-migrate, ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT and DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT to Production, and on the API Parcels__Store=FileSystem with Parcels__FileSystemRoot=/var/lib/passel/parcels, in the parcels volume. To tune one of the Web API settings below on the server, add it to the API's environment in a compose override kept outside the releases, such as /opt/passel/compose.local.yaml, and add that file to COMPOSE_FILE by its absolute path (COMPOSE_FILE=compose.yaml:/opt/passel/compose.local.yaml); the release directories are replaced on every deploy. These stay unset in the compose deployment, since each belongs to Azure or to Development and would change how the API signs in, exports or trusts headers: APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING, every AZURE_* variable, Database__ApiRoleObjectId, Authentication__Google__ClientSecret and ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED. Azure deployment Legacy (ADR 0003): this is the Azure deployment, which stays in the code but is no longer where Passel runs. aspire publish and aspire deploy add the Azure resources to the AppHost (Releasing and Deploying). DeployWebApi supplies everything below from the Deploy workflow's variables and secret; nothing needs typing in. Setting Secret Source in the workflow Description Azure:SubscriptionId, Azure:ResourceGroup, Azure:Location No AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP, AZURE_LOCATION Where Aspire deploys. The resource group must exist (Azure:AllowResourceGroupCreation is false), and the migration step needs the first two to find the job. Azure:CredentialSource No Always AzureCli The Azure CLI session that azure/login leaves behind Parameters:google-client-id No GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID The API's Authentication:Google:ClientId Parameters:google-extension-client-id No CHROME_EXTENSION_CLIENT_ID The API's Authentication:Google:AdditionalAudiences:0 Parameters:encoding-alphabet Yes ENCODING_ALPHABET (environment secret) Stored in Key Vault as encoding-alphabet; the container app reads it as the API's Encoding:Alphabet. Must never change once ids are in use. Deployment:ImageTag No GitVersion's version for the commit Azure only: the tag both images are pushed to the Azure registry with. Without it they are pushed as latest. The compose deployment's images are tagged by PublishImages instead. Deployment:ApiDomain No API_DOMAIN The API's custom domain. Empty for none; when set, the container app binds it and AllowedHosts includes it. Parameters:api-certificate-name No API_CERTIFICATE_NAME The managed certificate for the domain; empty for the first deployment with it. Only asked for when Deployment:ApiDomain is set. In Azure (legacy) the API's container gets: Variable Value ConnectionStrings__passel-db Host=<server>;Database=passel-db;Username=<the API identity's role>;Ssl Mode=Require, with no password ConnectionStrings__passel-blobs The storage account's blob endpoint (https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/), with no key: the API signs in as its identity, which has Storage Blob Data Contributor on the account and no other storage role. Aspire also sets the same URI as ConnectionStrings__passel_blobs and PASSEL_BLOBS_URI, which the API doesn't read. Encoding__Alphabet The Key Vault secret, through the API identity AllowedHosts The container app's default host name, localhost (the health probes send it) and the custom domain when there is one Authentication__Google__ClientId, Authentication__Google__AdditionalAudiences__0 From the parameters above APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING From the Application Insights resource AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_TOKEN_CREDENTIALS Set by Aspire, so the Entra tokens are for the API's managed identity ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED, HTTP_PORTS Set by Aspire for Container Apps ingress The migration job gets the database's connection string (as its own identity, an Entra administrator) and Database__ApiRole and Database__ApiRoleObjectId, the API identity's role name and object id. It gets no storage connection string and no role on the storage account: it never touches files. Web API Key Required Description ConnectionStrings:passel-db Yes PostgreSQL connection string. The AppHost provides it. Without a password (as in Azure) the API signs in with a Microsoft Entra token for its managed identity, and the user name, if missing, is taken from the token. ConnectionStrings:passel-blobs For files in Azure Azure Blob Storage, where uploaded files are kept when Parcels:Store is Auto (the default) or AzureBlob; the filesystem store ignores it. The AppHost provides it (Azurite locally). A connection string with an account key, or Azurite's UseDevelopmentStorage=true, is used as it is; a plain blob endpoint URI (as in Azure) signs in with the managed identity. Without it, and with Parcels:Store left at Auto, the API still starts, every file endpoint answers 503, and outside Development it logs a warning at startup. Authentication:Google:ClientId Outside Development The web client id: the main accepted token audience, and the client for development login. Without it every Google token is rejected; in Development the Dev scheme still works. Authentication:Google:ClientSecret No The web client secret. With it and the client id both set, Development offers the Scalar Login with Google banner. Authentication:Google:AdditionalAudiences No Other accepted audiences, for example the extension's client id Encoding:Alphabet No The Sqids alphabet for public ids. Changing it invalidates existing ids. OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT No Turns on OTLP export of logs, traces and metrics. The AppHost points it at the dashboard. Ignored when APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING is set. APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING No Sends logs, traces and metrics to Application Insights instead, with the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry distro. The Azure deployment sets it. RateLimits:CreatesPerMinute No Packets a user may create per minute. Default 30. RateLimits:ReadsPerMinute No Packet list and delete requests, and device lists, a user may make per minute. Default 120. RateLimits:StreamsPerMinute No Event streams a user may open per minute. Default 10. RateLimits:DeviceWritesPerMinute No Device registrations, renames, removals and push token changes a user may make per minute. Default 20. RateLimits:ParcelUploadsPerMinute No File uploads and discards a user may make per minute (parcel-uploads). Default 10. RateLimits:ParcelReadsPerMinute No File downloads and thumbnails a user may fetch per minute (parcel-reads). Default 600, since a feed page can show fifty thumbnails. Quotas:MaxPacketsPerUser No The most packets a user may have at once. Default 5000. Quotas:MaxBytesPerUser No The most bytes a user may have stored across their packet documents. Default 52428800 (50 MB). Uploaded files don't count here; see Quotas:MaxParcelBytesPerUser. Quotas:MaxParcelBytesPerUser No The most bytes of uploaded files a user may have at once: every file not deleted, sent or not, with an upload in progress counted at the size it declared. Default 524288000 (500 MB). Quotas:MaxPendingParcelsPerUser No The most files a user may have uploaded but not sent, from 1 to 1000; they expire after Parcels:UnattachedLifetime, so this bounds what an abandoned client leaves behind. Default 20. Quotas:MaxDevicesPerUser No The most devices a user may have registered at once, from 1 to 1000; the device list is not paged, so this also bounds its length. Default 20. Parcels:Store No Which store keeps the bytes of uploaded files: Auto (the default) uses Azure when ConnectionStrings:passel-blobs is set and has no store otherwise, so every file endpoint answers 503; AzureBlob uses Azure and stops the API at startup without the connection string; FileSystem keeps the files in Parcels:FileSystemRoot. Parcels:FileSystemRoot With FileSystem The directory the filesystem store keeps the files in: an absolute path on a local disk, never a network share, which the API's user can write. It holds a file per original and per thumbnail, named by the parcel id, and a .uploading directory for uploads in progress. It is created on the first upload if it is missing; make it a directory of its own rather than the root of a mount, whose lost+found the orphan scan would report on every run. Parcels:ContainerName No Azure only: the blob container files are kept in. The API creates it if it's missing. Default parcels. Parcels:MaxParcelBytes No The largest file one upload may carry, at most 1 GiB. Default 26214400 (25 MB). Above about 30 MB (Kestrel's default body limit), raise Kestrel:Limits:MaxRequestBodySize with it. Parcels:UnattachedLifetime No How long an uploaded file waits to be sent before it is deleted, from a second to seven days. Default 01:00:00. Parcels:UploadingGrace No How long an upload may stay unfinished (its instance stopped part way) before it is taken to have failed and deleted, from a second to a day, and shorter than Parcels:UnattachedLifetime. Default 00:15:00. Parcels:SweepEnabled No Whether the sweep runs. Off, deleted and expired files keep their bytes until it is on again. Default true. Parcels:SweepInterval No How often the sweep runs when nothing wakes it sooner (a delete wakes it at once), from a second to an hour. Default 00:05:00. Parcels:OrphanScanInterval No How often the sweep also looks for stored bytes with no file and files whose packet is gone, from a minute to seven days. Default 1.00:00:00. Parcels:OrphanBlobMinimumAge No How old stored bytes with no file must be before the orphan scan deletes them, up to seven days. Default 02:00:00. Parcels:SweepBatchSize No How many files the sweep expires or erases per batch, from 1 to 1000. Default 100. Parcels:ThumbnailSize No The longest side of a thumbnail in pixels, from 64 to 2048. Default 512. Parcels:MaxImagePixels No The most pixels an image may have to be decoded for a thumbnail; larger ones are kept as plain files. A PNG or GIF decodes at full size, four bytes a pixel, so this bounds the memory a decode takes. Default 40000000. Parcels:MaxImageDimension No The longest side an image may have to be decoded for a thumbnail. Default 16384. Parcels:DecodeSlotTimeout No How long an upload waits for the one image decode an instance runs at a time, up to a minute; an image still waiting then is stored as a plain file without a thumbnail, keeping its sniffed type. Default 00:00:05. Parcels:MaxConcurrentUploads No How many uploads one instance takes at once, from 1 to 64; the next waits five seconds and then gets 503. Default 4. EventStreams:MaxStreamsPerUser No Event streams one user may hold open on one instance; opening another closes their oldest. Default 5. EventStreams:MaxStreamsPerInstance No Event streams one instance holds open in total; beyond it the endpoint answers 503. Default 4000. AllowedHosts No The hosts the API answers to, separated by ;. appsettings.json sets the production host, api.passel.link; a deployment on another host overrides it, and must include the host its health probes use. Ignored in Development, which answers to any host. ForwardedHeaders:Enabled No Behind a reverse proxy, take the client address and scheme from X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto. Default false. Leave it off in Azure Container Apps: the deployment sets ASP.NET Core's own ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED there, and turning both on would apply the headers twice, letting a client choose the address the rate limits see. ForwardedHeaders:KnownProxies No The proxy addresses to accept those headers from, as a list. ForwardedHeaders:KnownNetworks No The proxy networks to accept those headers from, in CIDR notation, as a list. With neither list set, the headers are accepted from whatever connects directly, which is only safe when the proxy is the one way to reach the API. Cors:AllowedOrigins No The browser origins allowed to call the API across origins, as a list: the web app's, such as https://passel.link. Each is written as the browser sends it in the Origin header (scheme, host, and a port only when it isn't the default; no path, no trailing slash, no wildcard), and the API refuses to start with one that isn't. Empty by default, which allows no origin. The AppHost sets the web app's local origin. Cors:PreflightMaxAge No How long a browser may cache the answer to a preflight request. Default 00:10:00, at most two hours. Kestrel:Limits:MaxConcurrentConnections No The most open connections, event streams included. Default 5000. The rest of the Kestrel section binds too. LinkPreviews:Enabled No Whether the page of a new link is fetched for a preview. Default true. LinkPreviews:Timeout No How long one fetch attempt may take in all, redirects and body included. Default 00:00:05. LinkPreviews:MaxBodyBytes No The most bytes read from a page. Default 524288 (512 KB). LinkPreviews:MaxRedirects No How many redirects a fetch follows, each checked like the first URL. Default 3. LinkPreviews:MaxAttempts No How often a fetch is attempted before the link is left without a preview; only timeouts, connection failures and 429 or 5xx answers are retried. Default 3. LinkPreviews:RetryDelay No The wait before the second attempt; each later attempt waits that much longer again. Default 00:00:05. LinkPreviews:MaxConcurrentFetches No How many pages one instance fetches at the same time. Default 4. LinkPreviews:QueueCapacity No How many links may wait for a fetch on one instance; beyond it, new links go without a preview. Default 1000. Database:ApiRole No Only read by db-migrate: the role the API logs in as, which it grants the API's DML-only privileges. See Schema in production. Database:ApiRoleObjectId No Only read by db-migrate: the Microsoft Entra object id of the API's managed identity, so the role is created as its Entra principal. Outside Development, appsettings.Production.json keeps Npgsql's log of every command it runs to warnings, so production logs don't carry each SQL statement. Link previews are fetched after a link is created, behind guards that no setting loosens: http and https only, public addresses only, checked on every redirect. See Link previews. CORS is for the web app alone: the extension's host permissions bypass CORS, and the mobile app isn't a browser. An origin in Cors:AllowedOrigins may call the API with GET, POST and DELETE, sending Authorization, Content-Type and Accept, and Range and If-None-Match to resume or revalidate a file download, and may read Retry-After, Location, ETag, Content-Disposition, Content-Range, Accept-Ranges and Content-Length; credentials (cookies) are never allowed, since the clients send a bearer token. Preflight requests are answered ahead of authentication and rate limiting. Any other origin gets no CORS headers, so the browser keeps the answer from its page. Outside Development the API also sends HSTS. Rate limits are sliding one-minute windows counted per signed-in user (the sub claim), or per remote address for requests that aren't authenticated. A request over the limit gets a 429 problem with a Retry-After header. Quotas are checked before every create with one indexed aggregate over the user's packets. The byte quota counts the stored size of the packet documents, which PostgreSQL compresses when they're large, so it's a storage cap rather than an exact character count. A user at the packet limit gets a 429 problem; a packet that would pass the byte limit gets a 413 problem. Both say to delete packets. The device cap is checked only when an installation registers for the first time, so a device that is registered already is never refused; a user at the cap gets a 429 problem saying to remove a device. New installations registering at the same moment are all checked against the same count, so a burst can pass the cap by up to RateLimits:DeviceWritesPerMinute less one; raising that limit loosens the cap too. Lowering the cap removes nobody's devices. Uploads are checked against their own quotas, before the body is read and again once the file is stored: a file over Parcels:MaxParcelBytes or one that would pass Quotas:MaxParcelBytesPerUser gets a 413 problem, and an upload beyond Quotas:MaxPendingParcelsPerUser unsent files a 429 problem. Lowering a limit deletes no files. The upload endpoint sets the request body limit of its own requests to Parcels:MaxParcelBytes plus 64 KB for the multipart framing, and counts the file itself as it reads it. When the file limit is set above Kestrel's default of about 30 MB, raise Kestrel:Limits:MaxRequestBodySize with it; only the endpoint's own count is covered by the tests, because the test server enforces no body limit. When you run the API outside the AppHost, put these in src/webapi/Invex.Passel.WebApi/appsettings.Development.json. The file is git-ignored by the *.Development.json rule. Settings supplied by the AppHost take precedence over the file. Chrome extension src/chrome-extension/.env (template: .env.example) is only read by standalone builds; the AppHost supplies these values itself. Key Description API_URL The packets endpoint, for example https://localhost:7030/api/packets GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID The extension's OAuth client id DEV_SIGN_IN true lets a development build (npm run dev, npm run dev:watch) sign in as a development user through the API's Development-only Dev scheme, without Google; GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID may then be left empty. A minified build (npm run build) never has it. The AppHost sets it. Web app src/web/.env (template: .env.example) is only read by the dev server (npm run dev, npm run serve) outside the AppHost, which supplies these values itself; a production build (npm run build, BuildWebApp) needs none. See Web App. Deployed, the web image takes API_ORIGIN and GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID from its container's environment instead (The web image). Key Description API_URL The packets endpoint, for example https://localhost:7030/api/packets, served in /app/config.json. Its origin goes into the app's Content-Security-Policy. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID The Google OAuth web client id, served in /app/config.json, whose Authorized JavaScript origins must include the app's origin DEV_SIGN_IN true lets a development build (npm run dev) sign in as a development user through the API's Development-only Dev scheme, without Google; GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID may then be left empty. A minified build (npm run build) never has it. The AppHost sets it. PORT The dev server's port (npm run dev, npm run serve). Default 5245. The AppHost sets it. Mobile app src/mobile_app/.env (template: .env.example) is compiled in with --dart-define-from-file. Key Required Description API_BASE_URL Yes The API root as the device can reach it: http://localhost:5218 for a phone on USB (with adb reverse tcp:5218 tcp:5218), http://10.0.2.2:5218 for an emulator, or the dev tunnel URL. The production flavor requires https://; the development flavor allows http:// only to localhost, 127.0.0.1 and 10.0.2.2. SERVER_CLIENT_ID Unless DEV_USER is set The Google web client id APP_CLIENT_ID No The Android client id TUNNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN No A Dev Tunnels access token (devtunnel token <tunnel-id> --scopes connect), sent as X-Tunnel-Authorization: tunnel <token> with every request, for a tunnel that doesn't allow anonymous access. Development flavor only: the production flavor refuses to start with one. DEV_USER No Signs the development flavor in as this user through the API's Development-only Dev scheme (Authorization: Dev <user>) instead of Google, so no Google client is needed. The login page can sign in as any other user, and each user is a separate account. Development flavor only: the production flavor refuses to start with one. Build _atom/appsettings.json holds build parameter defaults; see Build Targets. The deployment's parameters are listed with DeployWebApi.

docs/reference/http-api.html.summary: HTTP API When the API runs locally in development, the interactive reference is at https://localhost:7030/scalar. This page summarises the contract. Every endpoint below requires Authorization: Bearer <Google ID token>. When the API runs in Development it also accepts Authorization: Dev <user-id>; see Run without Google. Browsers may call the API only from the origins in Cors:AllowedOrigins, which is where the web app is served from (Configuration). Requests may pass ?api-version=1; when it's omitted, version 1 is assumed. Errors use application/problem+json. Limits Each endpoint is rate limited per user, over a sliding window of one minute. The defaults are 30 creates, 120 list or delete requests (the device list counts here too), 10 event-stream connections, 20 device writes (registrations, renames, removals and push token changes), 10 file uploads and discards (parcel-uploads), and 600 file downloads and thumbnails (parcel-reads) per minute; see Configuration. A request over the limit gets 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (in seconds) and a problem body. Each user also has a quota: by default 5,000 packets and 50 MB of stored packets. A create at the packet limit gets 429, and one that would pass the byte limit gets 413 Content Too Large; the problem detail says which, and that deleting packets frees the quota. Neither has a Retry-After, because only a delete changes the outcome. In the same way, a user may have 20 devices; registering another gets 429 without a Retry-After until one is removed. The cap is not exact: registrations of new installations sent at the same moment are each checked against the count before any of them is stored, so a burst can take a user past it, by at most one less than the device-writes rate limit. Uploaded files have quotas of their own, apart from the packet quota: a file may be at most 25 MB, a user's files at most 500 MB together, and a user may have 20 files uploaded but not yet sent. An upload of a larger file gets 413 ("File too large"), one that would pass the storage limit 413 ("Storage limit reached"), and one beyond the unsent files 429 ("Too many unsent files"), none with a Retry-After: sending, discarding or deleting files, or waiting for unsent ones to expire after an hour, is what frees the quota. Like the packet quota, these are checked before the file is stored and can be passed by uploads sent at the same moment. When file storage can't be reached, the file endpoints answer 503 with Retry-After, and packets, devices and the event stream keep working; see Parcels. A request body the API cannot read at all (malformed JSON, a missing or unknown $type, an unknown enum value, a missing required field) gets 400 with a plain problem; one it can read but refuses gets 400 with a validation problem, whose errors are keyed by field. Packets Packets are a tagged union with a $type discriminator. $type doesn't have to be the first property. $type Fields Link id, createdAt, name (nullable), url, preview (nullable; see Link previews) Text id, createdAt, title (nullable), body File id, createdAt, fileName (nullable), contentType, parcelId, isImage. Created from an uploaded file; see Parcels. id is an opaque string (a Sqids-encoded Guid). createdAt is when the packet was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC (for example 2026-10-22T11:03:08.1234567+00:00); it is returned, never sent. Link previews After a link is created, the API fetches its page in the background and reads what the page says about itself: the Open Graph tags first (og:title, og:description, og:image), the Twitter card tags next, and the <title> and <meta name="description"> last. What it finds is stored on the link and returned as its preview: { "title": "Example Domain", "description": "This domain is for use in illustrative examples in documents.", "imageUrl": "https://example.com/images/og.png", "fetchedAt": "2026-10-22T11:03:10.1234567+00:00" } title, description and imageUrl are each nullable, but never all three at once; fetchedAt is when the page was read. The title keeps at most 256 characters and the description 512. imageUrl is the page's image as an absolute http or https URL; the API has not fetched it, so clients load it as they would any third-party image. preview is null on the create response and in the packet-created event, because the page is fetched after the create has returned. When the fetch finds something, the link is announced again as a packet-updated event, and the list shows the preview from then on. When the page gives nothing, is not HTML, cannot be reached within a few attempts, or is on a private network the API refuses to fetch from, preview stays null for good: nothing is stored or announced about the failure. Links created before previews existed have none. GET /api/packets Returns the caller's packets, newest first, 50 per page. Query Description cursor The nextCursor from the previous page. An invalid cursor returns 400. { "packets": [ { "$type": "Link", "id": "…", "createdAt": "2026-10-22T11:03:08.1234567+00:00", "name": "Example", "url": "https://example.com" } ], "nextCursor": "…" } nextCursor is null on the last page. POST /api/packets Creates a packet and returns it, with its id and createdAt, as 200 OK. Nullable fields must be sent explicitly, even as null. { "$type": "Text", "title": null, "body": "Hello from my laptop" } Rule Limit name and title At most 256 characters url Absolute http or https URL, at most 2048 characters body Not blank, at most 65,536 characters Request body At most 256 KB A File packet sends a file uploaded to POST /api/parcels, by the parcelId the upload answered with. fileName may be left out (or null) to keep the name the file was uploaded with, or given to send it under another; it is made safe the way an uploaded name is. The type and isImage always come from the upload. { "$type": "File", "parcelId": "qrjMmYBVnK8m3coMo0hiMeN", "fileName": "screenshot.png" } Rule Limit parcelId A file the caller uploaded, has not discarded, and has not sent yet fileName At most 256 characters A parcelId that isn't one of the caller's uploaded files (another user's, one still uploading, one discarded or expired, or not an id at all) gets 400 with a validation problem on parcelId. A missing file and another user's get the same answer, so ids can't be probed. A file that is already in a packet gets 409 Conflict ("File already sent"): a file is sent once, so upload it again to send it twice. Two sends of the same file at the same moment get one 200 and one 409. Validation failures return a validation problem keyed by field. A create that would exceed the caller's quota returns 429 or 413; see Limits. A File packet counts against the packet quota for its name only; its bytes count against the file quota when uploaded. DELETE /api/packets/{id} Returns 204 and erases the packet; nothing of it is kept. Returns 404 if the id is malformed, the packet doesn't exist, or it belongs to someone else. Deleting a File packet deletes its file with it: from that moment the file's download and thumbnail answer 404, and its bytes are erased from storage within seconds (at most five minutes, the sweep interval). GET /api/packets/events A text/event-stream of the caller's changes: Event Data resync Empty. Sent first, and whenever events may have been missed. Fetch the list again. packet-created The packet, in the same shape as a list item packet-updated The packet, in the same shape as packet-created, after a change to it: today, a link whose preview arrived. A client that doesn't handle the event loses nothing by ignoring it; the next list shows the change. packet-deleted { "id": "…" } ping Heartbeat, after 20 seconds without other events There are no event ids. To recover after a disconnect, reconnect and handle the resync. The server may close a stream at any time, for example on shutdown or when the client falls behind. The first event carries a retry: field, a reconnection delay between 2 and 6 seconds chosen per stream, so clients that honour it (such as EventSource) reconnect spread out after a restart. Other clients should reconnect with jittered backoff. A stream also ends when the token that opened it would stop validating (its exp plus five minutes of clock skew, so about an hour for a Google ID token) and after a day at most. Reconnect with a fresh token. A user may hold five streams open per API instance; opening a sixth closes the oldest. When an instance has no room for another stream at all, the request gets 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After. Devices A device is one installation of a client (the Android app, the extension in one browser profile, the web app in one browser) signed in as one user. Clients register on every start and may give the API a push token, which the API will use to tell the device that something arrived (push sending is not built yet). Every device endpoint lives under /api/devices and acts only on the caller's own devices; another user's device is answered as a missing one, with 404. Field Description id The device's public id, opaque like a packet id. Keep the id your registration returned: it is how the client tells itself apart in the list. name What the user calls the device, at most 64 characters platform android, extension or web createdAt When the installation first registered, in UTC lastSeenAt When it last registered, in UTC pushUpdatedAt When its push token was last set, in UTC, or null when it has none. The token itself is never returned. { "id": "…", "name": "Pixel 9", "platform": "android", "createdAt": "2026-11-04T09:30:00.1234567+00:00", "lastSeenAt": "2026-11-07T08:12:45.7654321+00:00", "pushUpdatedAt": null } POST /api/devices Registers the installation and returns the device. { "installationId": "6f1c2a9e-4b7d-4e2a-9c3f-0d8e5b7a1c24", "name": "Pixel 9", "platform": "android" } The installation id is the client's own: generate it once per installation (a random UUID will do), keep it in the client's storage, and send it with every registration. That makes registering idempotent: An installation id the caller has not registered makes a new device: 201 Created, with a Location of /api/devices/{id}. One the caller has registered returns the same device as 200 OK, with lastSeenAt moved on. The name sent is ignored, because the user may have renamed the device since; it is only the name of a new device. One the caller has registered with another platform gets 409 Conflict, whose detail names the client it is registered for. Registrations of one installation sent at the same moment all get the same device: one gets 201 and the rest 200. The same installation id under another account is a separate device of that account. Signing out and in as someone else therefore adds a device to the second account and leaves the first account's device where it was, to be removed from its settings. A removed device is gone: when its installation registers again, it gets a new device with a new id. Rule Limit installationId 16 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, - or _ name Not blank, at most 64 characters without the whitespace around it (which is trimmed), no control characters platform android, extension or web Request body At most 16 KB, on every device endpoint A new device beyond the caller's device cap gets 429; see Limits. An installation that is registered already is never refused. GET /api/devices Returns all of the caller's devices, in the order they registered. The list is not paged; the device cap bounds it. { "devices": [ { "id": "…", "name": "Pixel 9", "platform": "android", "createdAt": "…", "lastSeenAt": "…", "pushUpdatedAt": "…" } ] } PATCH /api/devices/{id} Renames the device and returns it. The name follows the registration rules. { "name": "Work phone" } DELETE /api/devices/{id} Returns 204 and removes the device with its push token. Returns 404 if the id is malformed, the device doesn't exist, or it belongs to someone else. PUT /api/devices/{id}/push Gives the device its push token, replacing any it had, and returns 204. Android devices send their Firebase Cloud Messaging registration token: { "$type": "Fcm", "token": "…" } Extension and web devices send their Web Push subscription, which is PushSubscription.toJSON() with the discriminator added (expirationTime is ignored): { "$type": "WebPush", "endpoint": "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/…", "keys": { "p256dh": "…", "auth": "…" } } Rule Limit Kind Fcm on an android device, WebPush on an extension or web device; the other kind is a validation problem keyed $type token 1 to 4,096 printable ASCII characters, no spaces endpoint An absolute https URL of at most 2,048 characters, on a host name (not an IP address) and the default port, without credentials keys.p256dh Base64url of a 65-byte uncompressed P-256 public key keys.auth Base64url of a 16-byte secret Send the token again whenever the client starts or the platform gives it a new one; pushUpdatedAt then shows how fresh it is. A push token belongs to one device at a time. When a token (an FCM token, or a subscription's endpoint) is set on a device while another device holds it, under this account or any other, the other device loses it. That is what happens when one installation signs in as another account: its token follows the new account, and the old account's device stops receiving pushes. Nothing in the response says that a token moved. A body without $type, such as PushSubscription.toJSON() sent as it is, gets 400. DELETE /api/devices/{id}/push Removes the device's push token and returns 204, also when it had none. Returns 404 for a device the caller doesn't have. Conflicts A registration, a rename, or setting or removing a push token, that keeps colliding with other requests changing the same device at the same moment gets 409 Conflict with a problem saying to send it again. That is safe: each of these requests can be repeated without a different outcome. Registrations of one installation never collide with each other this way. Parcels A parcel is an uploaded file. Sending a file takes two requests: upload it to POST /api/parcels, then create a File packet with the parcelId the upload answered with (POST /api/packets). Every parcel endpoint lives under /api/parcels and acts only on the caller's own files; another user's file is answered as a missing one, with 404. A file is the packet's from the moment it is sent: it lives as long as its packet, and deleting the packet deletes it. A file uploaded but not sent within an hour is deleted. Field Description parcelId The file's public id, opaque like a packet id, and the parcelId of the File packet that sends it fileName The name the file was uploaded with, made safe (see below), or null when nothing of it was left contentType The type read from the file's first bytes: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp, application/pdf, or application/octet-stream for anything else. The type the client declared is never used. size The file's size in bytes isImage Whether the file decoded as a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image. Only an image has a thumbnail. width, height The image's size in pixels as it is displayed, after its EXIF orientation; null when it is not an image { "parcelId": "qrjMmYBVnK8m3coMo0hiMeN", "fileName": "screenshot.png", "contentType": "image/png", "size": 48213, "isImage": true, "width": 1280, "height": 720 } An image larger than 40 megapixels, or more than 16,384 pixels on a side, is not decoded: it is stored with its type but as isImage: false, with no thumbnail and with width and height null. So is one that fails to decode, and one uploaded while the server's image decoder stays busy with other uploads for more than five seconds (Parcels:DecodeSlotTimeout). POST /api/parcels Uploads one file as multipart/form-data, with one part named file that carries a file name, which is what a browser's FormData and Flutter's MultipartRequest send: POST /api/parcels Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=x --x Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="screenshot.png" Content-Type: image/png <the bytes> --x-- The part's Content-Type is ignored. The file name is made safe before it is kept: only what follows the last / or \ is kept, control characters and the characters that reorder text (such as U+202E) are removed, it is normalised (NFC), and spaces and dots are trimmed from both ends. A name with nothing left is null. Returns the file as 201 Created, with a Location of /api/parcels/{parcelId}. Status When 201 The file is stored 400 A validation problem on file: no multipart/form-data boundary, no part named file with a file name, an empty file, more than one part, or a body that isn't valid multipart. On fileName: the safe name is longer than 256 characters. 413 The file is over 25 MB ("File too large"; a body that says it is longer is refused before it is read), or it would take the caller's files past 500 MB ("Storage limit reached") 415 The body is not multipart/form-data 429 The caller has 20 files uploaded but not sent ("Too many unsent files", no Retry-After), or the parcel-uploads rate limit (with Retry-After) 503 Too many uploads at once on the server ("File storage is busy", Retry-After: 5), file storage can't be reached ("File storage unavailable", Retry-After: 30), or the upload took so long that it was discarded ("Upload discarded"); send it again A body sent without a Content-Length (chunked) is accepted, and counts as 25 MB against the storage limit until it is stored. GET /api/parcels/{id} Returns the file's bytes as they were uploaded, with its sniffed Content-Type. Header Value ETag The SHA-256 of the bytes, in lower-case hex, quoted. Send it as If-None-Match and an unchanged file (they never change) gets 304 Not Modified. Last-Modified When the file was uploaded Accept-Ranges bytes: a Range request gets 206 Partial Content, and one outside the file 416 Range Not Satisfiable. If-Range is honoured. Content-Disposition inline for an image that decoded and for a PDF, attachment for anything else, so an uploaded page or script is saved rather than opened. Always with the file's name, as filename* in UTF-8 and as an ASCII filename for clients that only read that (file.png and so on when the file has no name). Returns 404 if the id is malformed, the file doesn't exist, belongs to someone else, is still uploading, or has been discarded, expired or deleted with its packet. A browser that opens a PDF under Content-Security-Policy: sandbox may refuse to show it; the file is then downloaded instead. GET /api/parcels/{id}/thumbnail Returns the image's thumbnail: a WebP of at most 512 pixels on its longest side (smaller images keep their size), the first frame of an animated image, turned upright by its EXIF orientation. Its ETag is the file's with the thumbnail size added, and If-None-Match gets 304; it has no ranges. Returns 404 as the download does, and for a file that has no thumbnail (isImage: false). DELETE /api/parcels/{id} Discards a file that hasn't been sent and returns 204. It is unavailable at once, and its bytes are erased from storage within seconds. A file that is in a packet gets 409 Conflict ("Delete the item instead"): delete its packet instead, which deletes the file with it. Returns 404 for a file the caller doesn't have. Discards count against the parcel-uploads rate limit. Headers and caching Every answer of a parcel endpoint, its problems and 404s included, carries Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none', X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, so nothing uploaded runs as a page on the API's origin or is read as another type. A download or thumbnail (200, 206 or 304) is Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable with Vary: Authorization, since a file never changes; every other answer is Cache-Control: no-store. File bodies are never compressed, so Content-Length and ranges always hold. The 401, the rate limit's 429 and the 415 for a body that isn't multipart are answered before the endpoint runs, and carry none of these. From a browser, the web app's origin may send Range and If-None-Match and read ETag, Content-Disposition, Content-Range, Accept-Ranges, Content-Length and Location; see Configuration. Privacy The original is stored and returned byte for byte, so a photo keeps its EXIF metadata, GPS position included, for whoever downloads it with the owner's token. Only the thumbnail is stripped: it carries no EXIF, XMP or colour profile. Delete a file (or its packet) to erase it: the storage keeps no deleted copy, neither a soft-deleted blob nor an earlier version. Other endpoints Endpoint Auth Description GET /health None Readiness: every health check. File storage is not one of them, so a storage outage leaves the API ready. GET /alive None Liveness GET /auth/login, /auth/logout, /auth/me Development only Cookie login for Scalar. /auth/login answers 503 when the Google client isn't configured.

index.html.summary: Passel Passel sends links and text between your devices. Push something from your browser and it shows up on your phone, live. The repository holds the apps that share one API: Component Stack Source Web API ASP.NET Core (.NET 10), Marten on PostgreSQL, hosted locally by .NET Aspire src/webapi Chrome Extension TypeScript, Manifest V3, esbuild src/chrome-extension Web App TypeScript, Preact, esbuild; also the landing, privacy and terms pages src/web Mobile App Flutter (Android), Riverpod src/mobile_app Builds, tests and docs are driven by Atom; see Build Targets. Start here Install the prerequisites, then run dotnet tool restore and dotnet atom SetupDevEnvironment to check them. Set up the Google OAuth clients the apps sign in with. Run everything locally with the Aspire AppHost.
